title: Resolving User Intent
description: Use when a request contains ambiguous goals, unstated constraints, conflicting stakeholders, or decisions that would cause competent teams to build materially different products.
antiTriggers: a fully specified deterministic command
a wording preference that cannot change behavior
steps: Separate user facts from interpretations and unknowns.
Classify unknowns as blocking, material, or safely deferrable.
Ask one decision-sized question and bind the answer to the intent artifact.
Stop only when scope-changing assumptions have authenticated ownership.
checks: No material assumption is silently invented.
Every success measure is observable.
Scope, non-goals, constraints, and decision owners are explicit.
failures: Treating chat history as confirmed intent.
Asking broad questions that combine multiple decisions.

title: Decomposing Multi-Domain Work
description: Use when one request spans independent product, engineering, design, security, data, legal, or operational subsystems that cannot be specified and verified as one bounded change.
antiTriggers: one bounded component with a single verification surface
tasks that only differ by file location
steps: Identify outcome boundaries and trust boundaries before technical layers.
Separate work that can fail or be approved independently.
Define typed handoffs and shared invariants between domains.
Order only true dependencies and leave independent branches parallel.
checks: Each subproject can be rejected independently.
Every cross-domain handoff has an owner and schema.
No circular ownership remains.
failures: Splitting by arbitrary file count.
Creating one giant specification for unrelated subsystems.

title: Routing the Capability Graph
description: Use when the system must translate confirmed intent, failed gates, missing artifacts, risks, and tools into the smallest safe set of outcome capabilities and techniques.
antiTriggers: the exact technique and provider were explicitly selected
provider installation before the desired outcome is known
steps: Retrieve outcome candidates from intent and current gate gaps.
Apply hard policy filters before any utility score.
Retrieve techniques by triggers, anti-triggers, inputs, and outputs.
Freeze the minimal executable route with inclusion and exclusion reasons.
checks: Quarantined providers are never activated.
Same semantic input produces the same route hash.
Every selected step closes a typed gap.
failures: Ranking providers before capability retrieval.
Using a high score to override missing tools or trust blockers.

title: Composing Technique Workflows
description: Use when one outcome requires multiple specialized techniques with branch, join, parallel, retry, or rollback relationships rather than a single linear skill invocation.
antiTriggers: one technique produces the complete verified outcome
a sequence exists only for presentation convenience
steps: Resolve required and optional technique relations.
Compute the smallest closure that produces all target artifacts and evidence.
Group independent nodes for parallel execution and preserve join conditions.
Attach retry, rollback, and stop paths to the exact node that owns them.
checks: The DAG is acyclic unless an explicit recovery loop is typed.
Every join names required upstream receipts.
Removing any selected node would leave a documented gap.
failures: Turning every dependency into a sequential step.
Hiding optional work inside a mandatory node.

title: Resolving Skill Conflicts
description: Use when candidate techniques, providers, policy profiles, ownership rules, or tool effects cannot safely coexist in the same execution route.
antiTriggers: alternatives are compatible and can run independently
a provider is merely lower ranked without a conflict
steps: Classify conflict as semantic, resource, authority, state, or side-effect conflict.
Determine whether ordering, isolation, substitution, or human choice can resolve it.
Prefer the option preserving the target outcome with the least new authority.
Record excluded alternatives and invalidation consequences.
checks: No conflicting writer owns the same output slot.
Resolution does not weaken assurance silently.
Human choice is required for value trade-offs, not guessed.
failures: Treating low similarity as conflict.
Choosing the highest-trust provider without checking incompatible effects.

title: Planning Parallel Agent Work
description: Use when several work units are independent enough to execute concurrently but still need deterministic ownership, coverage, resource locks, and verified joins.
antiTriggers: shared mutable state cannot be isolated
the next task requires the previous task output
steps: Derive work units from dependency and change graphs.
Assign one owner and output lock per unit.
Define context packs that omit unrelated sibling work.
Join only after every unit has a trusted completion receipt.
checks: No output target has two active writers.
Coverage ledger accounts for every scoped unit.
Join failure leaves resumable state.
failures: Parallelizing coupled edits to the same invariant.
Sharing one giant context between all workers.

title: Selecting the Minimum Provider Set
description: Use when a route has several procedural, knowledge, MCP, or tool providers and must choose the smallest trusted combination that satisfies all outputs and evidence obligations.
antiTriggers: the selected technique has one mandatory provider
provider choice is fixed by tenant policy
steps: Filter by tenant, status, freshness, license, tools, and trust blockers.
Build coverage sets for required outputs, evidence, and tool operations.
Solve for minimum provider coverage with conflict and token penalties.
Record why each remaining provider was excluded.
checks: No selected provider is redundant for the current route.
Knowledge mappings are not counted as procedural execution.
Credential scope is minimal.
failures: Selecting one provider of every kind by default.
Treating popularity as trust or necessity.

title: Explaining Route Decisions
description: Use when a human or agent needs a concise, auditable explanation of why techniques and providers were selected, excluded, blocked, or deferred.
antiTriggers: no route has been compiled
raw internal scoring would expose secrets or private content
steps: Summarize target outcomes and hard constraints first.
Explain selected steps in dependency order using evidence-backed reasons.
Group exclusions by anti-trigger, policy, missing tool, conflict, or lower marginal value.
Expose uncertainty and the exact action required to unblock execution.
checks: Explanation can be read in under one minute.
Every selected and rejected candidate is accounted for.
No private prompt or secret is disclosed.
failures: Dumping raw score vectors without interpretation.
Claiming a choice was optimal when search was bounded.

title: Compiling Global Context
description: Use when an agent request must combine system policy, task state, skill sections, code, artifacts, memory, tools, and references under one hard model-context budget.
antiTriggers: the complete request is already far below every category budget
archival storage with no model invocation
steps: Reserve output and safety capacity before selecting inputs.
Count every category with one model-specific accounting provider.
Select required items first and rank optional items by route value.
Emit a context receipt and omission manifest for every excluded source.
checks: Total input is below the hard limit.
No source disappears without an omission record.
The receipt binds hashes of all included sections.
failures: Budgeting only skill text.
Truncating the tail without knowing which evidence was removed.

title: Enforcing Context Budgets
description: Use when planned context, tool schemas, model output reserve, or retrieved artifacts may exceed tenant, route, model, or skill-specific token limits.
antiTriggers: token measurement is unavailable and no conservative fallback exists
a storage-size limit unrelated to model context
steps: Resolve the strictest applicable model, tenant, route, and section limits.
Apply calibrated safety margins from observed tokenizer error.
Reject required content that cannot fit rather than silently clipping it.
Record category usage, remaining reserve, and overflow blockers.
checks: Runtime cannot submit an over-budget request.
Output reserve is never consumed by input selection.
Estimator error is measured after provider usage is reported.
failures: Deriving budget from lifecycle ordinal.
Using bytes divided by four without a safety margin.

title: Selecting Skill Sections
description: Use when a technique package contains overview, procedure, decisions, verification, failure modes, examples, or references and only a subset is needed for the current operation.
antiTriggers: the complete skill is shorter than the section-selection overhead
the requested section digest is stale
steps: Classify the operation as planning, execution, verification, recovery, or unfamiliar transfer.
Select mandatory overview and the minimum operation-specific sections.
Add examples or references only when uncertainty justifies their cost.
Bind section IDs, digests, token counts, and omitted sections into the route.
checks: No executable script is materialized as instruction text.
Selected section hashes match the provider manifest.
Median selected section count remains bounded.
failures: Loading all references for routine work.
Selecting examples instead of the required verification contract.

title: Projecting Artifact Deltas
description: Use when an agent needs current artifact state and changes since a checkpoint without receiving full historical artifacts and superseded versions.
antiTriggers: no checkpoint exists and the full artifact is explicitly required
the artifact content is smaller than its projection
steps: Resolve active artifact versions and requested dependency depth.
Compare content and envelope hashes with the checkpoint.
Emit changed fields, invalidations, and unchanged references separately.
Provide explicit fetch handles for omitted full bodies.
checks: Invalidated and superseded artifacts are never projected as active.
Reference depth is enforced.
Every delta identifies its source and current hash.
failures: Sending the complete history for one changed field.
Using timestamps instead of content identity.

title: Retrieving Semantic Code Symbols
description: Use when an agent must orient in a large codebase or fetch one implementation body by stable symbol identity, content hash, dependency, test, or call-site relation.
antiTriggers: a tiny file can be read safely in full
the language adapter cannot identify symbol boundaries
steps: Build or update a language-specific symbol graph incrementally.
Return compact IDs, signatures, hashes, and graph neighbors for orientation.
Fetch bodies only for explicitly requested symbol IDs and expected hashes.
Reject stale requests and include directly relevant tests and call sites.
checks: Symbol IDs remain stable across body-only edits.
Stale content hashes are rejected.
Permission boundaries apply before retrieval.
failures: Using line numbers as permanent identity.
Dumping the whole repository map every turn.

title: Distilling Tool Output
description: Use when test, compiler, browser, database, or terminal output is too large for model context but must remain retrievable and evidentially complete.
antiTriggers: the raw output is already concise
the output contains binary data requiring a specialized parser
steps: Store raw bytes in content-addressed evidence storage.
Classify output type and locate failures, warnings, stacks, and relevant ranges.
Create a bounded summary with command, status, duration, and omission notes.
Bind the summary to the raw digest and retrieval URI.
checks: Failure-causing ranges remain in the summary.
Raw output hash is verifiable.
Secrets are redacted before model delivery.
failures: Keeping only the final line of a multi-cause failure.
Letting a summary replace the raw evidence artifact.

title: Consolidating Project Memory
description: Use when decisions, blockers, conventions, and stable summaries must survive across tasks without treating conversation transcript as the project source of truth.
antiTriggers: ephemeral reasoning has no future decision value
the source artifacts are currently invalidated
steps: Classify information into active, task, project, or archive tiers.
Summarize only stable decisions with source IDs and hashes.
Expire or invalidate summaries when any source hash changes.
Select fresh memory by tier priority and request budget.
checks: Every summary has traceable sources.
Stale memory is excluded automatically.
Archive transcripts are never treated as authoritative state.
failures: Saving model speculation as a decision.
Keeping summaries after upstream artifacts change.

title: Calibrating Token Estimates
description: Use when estimated token counts differ systematically from provider-reported usage across models, content classes, languages, or tool schemas.
antiTriggers: the provider exposes an exact offline tokenizer already in use
one isolated observation is the only evidence
steps: Record estimated and actual usage with model version and content class.
Compute absolute and relative error without storing sensitive content.
Update bounded calibration factors using recent weighted observations.
Increase safety margin when uncertainty or model drift rises.
checks: Calibration cannot reduce safety below policy minimum.
p95 error is reported by model family.
Old model versions do not calibrate new versions silently.
failures: Optimizing the mean while hiding large tail errors.
Mixing message, text, and tool-schema observations.

title: Issuing Trusted Execution Receipts
description: Use when a command, test, scanner, brokered tool, or sandbox run must produce evidence whose pass status and digest cannot be chosen by the requesting agent.
antiTriggers: a human opinion is the evidence type
the provider is not authorized for the requested evidence method
steps: Authorize the evidence type and bind the request to a subject hash.
Execute through a trusted provider with bounded resources.
Derive status, output digest, timing, and environment from actual execution.
Sign or content-address the immutable receipt before returning metadata.
checks: Caller cannot set pass status or digest.
Receipt subject matches current semantic revision.
Raw evidence remains independently retrievable.
failures: Accepting a label-only security review.
Letting the worker also act as evidence issuer.

title: Validating Evidence Freshness
description: Use when a gate, artifact verification, finding closure, or release decision depends on evidence that may target an old revision, artifact hash, provider version, or environment.
antiTriggers: the evidence is informational and cannot change a decision
no subject identity is available
steps: Resolve the exact subject revision, hashes, and policy version required.
Verify receipt integrity, issuer authority, method, age, and environment.
Reject evidence whose upstream dependencies have changed.
Record per-rule accepted evidence and stale rejection reasons.
checks: A stale passing receipt cannot open a gate.
Freshness rules vary by assurance and evidence type.
Clock time is not used as the only identity signal.
failures: Checking only the evidence type string.
Reusing a review after the reviewed artifact changed.

title: Managing Artifact Lineage
description: Use when artifacts consume, replace, verify, invalidate, or derive from other versioned artifacts and downstream state must remain explainable and fresh.
antiTriggers: ephemeral notes with no downstream consumer
independent artifacts with no dependency relation
steps: Validate typed dependencies and active version slots before write.
Record content hash and immutable lifecycle envelope separately.
Maintain supersession links and dependency hashes in both directions.
Invalidate downstream artifacts and proof when an upstream subject changes.
checks: The artifact graph remains acyclic.
Exactly one active version exists per typed slot.
Tampering with lifecycle metadata is detectable.
failures: Treating hash as protection when metadata is outside the hash.
Leaving verified descendants active after supersession.

title: Invalidating Dependent Proof
description: Use when a semantic change, artifact supersession, provider substitution, policy change, or source revision makes previously accepted downstream proof unsafe to reuse.
antiTriggers: a cosmetic change does not affect any proof input
the dependency graph has no path to accepted evidence
steps: Identify changed semantic subjects and old hashes.
Traverse artifact, route, context, provider, and evidence dependencies.
Mark affected receipts and gates stale without deleting audit history.
Compute the minimal rerun plan needed to regain assurance.
checks: Invalidation is transitive and deterministic.
Historical proof remains visible but cannot satisfy current policy.
Unaffected branches stay valid.
failures: Invalidating the whole project for a local change.
Deleting old evidence instead of marking it stale.

title: Enforcing Review Separation
description: Use when artifact, code, finding, provider, or release approval requires independent review across principal, role, team, or trust-domain boundaries.
antiTriggers: A0 prototype policy explicitly permits self-review
the action is a reversible draft with no assurance claim
steps: Resolve producer, resolver, evaluator, closer, and signer trust domains.
Apply assurance-specific role and independence constraints.
Reject alternate IDs controlled by the same trust domain.
Bind the authorized reviewer and evidence set to the reviewed subject.
checks: Producer cannot be sole verifier for critical work.
Reviewer authority is scoped to tenant and artifact type.
Separation remains true after role delegation.
failures: Comparing display names instead of authenticated principals.
Assuming two service accounts are independent.

title: Binding Approvals to Actions
description: Use when an irreversible, high-risk, scope-changing, or trust-changing operation requires a human decision that cannot be replayed for another payload or state.
antiTriggers: a read-only operation with no external effect
an automated policy decision that requires no human value judgment
steps: Canonicalize the complete action envelope and current semantic snapshot.
Issue a one-time capability to an authenticated human principal.
Bind expiry, tenant, policy version, and payload digest.
Consume atomically and record revocation or replay attempts.
checks: Changing any argument makes the approval invalid.
Agent principals cannot mint human approvals.
Consumed or revoked capabilities cannot be reused.
failures: Using a guessable confirmation phrase.
Binding only an action name while omitting payload fields.

title: Recovering Interrupted Runs
description: Use when a skill, task, context compilation, tool execution, or release workflow stops after partial progress and must resume without duplicating side effects or trusting stale workers.
antiTriggers: the operation is atomic and has not started
the previous run completed with a terminal receipt
steps: Load the last committed state, lease, coverage, and output locks.
Reclaim only expired work using a higher fencing sequence.
Verify completed receipts and identify uncommitted side effects.
Resume the minimal remaining units with idempotency keys.
checks: Old workers cannot complete after reclamation.
Completed side effects are not repeated.
Recovery itself has an audit receipt.
failures: Restarting the whole workflow blindly.
Trusting local worker memory after lease expiry.

title: Auditing Agent Actions
description: Use when model decisions, tool calls, approvals, artifact mutations, provider selections, or evidence issuance must be reconstructed without storing secrets or unverifiable narrative.
antiTriggers: high-volume debug telemetry with no audit value
raw secret-bearing payloads that policy forbids storing
steps: Assign request, route, context, run, tool, evidence, and gate correlation IDs.
Record authenticated principal, action type, subject hashes, and result code.
Append to a tamper-evident chain or transparency checkpoint.
Expose bounded query views without leaking protected payloads.
checks: Every state mutation has an audit event.
Chain tampering is detectable.
Metrics labels exclude private high-cardinality IDs.
failures: Using chat prose as the audit log.
Logging secret values for convenience.

title: Writing Agent Skills with TDD
description: Use when creating or changing an agent skill whose behavior, routing, discipline, or technique must improve over a measurable baseline rather than merely sound persuasive.
antiTriggers: project-specific instructions that are not reusable
a mechanical rule better enforced entirely in code
steps: Write pressure or application scenarios before the skill.
Run the baseline without the candidate and capture exact failures.
Write the smallest skill addressing observed failures.
Rerun, close new loopholes, and preserve the evidence matrix.
checks: A failing baseline exists.
Candidate improvement is measured on the same cases and seeds.
No critical regression is hidden by aggregate score.
failures: Writing a complete skill before observing failure.
Using one successful example as validation.

title: Benchmarking Skill Utility
description: Use when deciding whether a skill or provider should be promoted, quarantined, selected, or retired based on paired task outcomes, quality, token cost, and uncertainty.
antiTriggers: single anecdotal success without a baseline
production promotion without paired runs
steps: Pin the skill version, corpus, models, seeds, tools, and policy.
Run baseline and candidate on an identical matrix.
Derive executable metrics and independent semantic judgments.
Store confidence, failure clusters, token deltas, and decision provenance.
checks: Producer cannot self-report decisive metrics.
Confidence lower bounds govern promotion.
Utility remains segmented by model and task class.
failures: Comparing runs on different case sets.
Averaging away critical failures.

title: Detecting Skill Regression
description: Use when a skill, policy profile, provider dependency, model version, or section change may reduce completion rate, quality, safety, routing accuracy, or token efficiency.
antiTriggers: no behavior-affecting content changed
the skill has no prior validated baseline
steps: Resolve affected benchmark and transfer-test slices.
Run paired evaluations across supported model families.
Cluster failures by trigger, route, procedure, verification, and tool interaction.
Quarantine or roll back when confidence shows harmful change.
checks: Same corpus and seeds are used.
Model-specific regressions are not hidden by global averages.
Rollback target is content-addressed.
failures: Testing only the model used by the author.
Ignoring token inflation when quality is flat.

title: Detecting Semantic Skill Duplication
description: Use when several skills or providers may express the same trigger, mechanism, outputs, evaluation surface, or benchmark coverage under different names.
antiTriggers: two techniques share an outcome but use distinct mechanisms
exact duplicates already match by content hash
steps: Compare exact and normalized structural signatures.
Measure trigger, output, procedure mechanism, and benchmark overlap separately.
Preserve alternatives when trade-offs or failure modes differ.
Require human merge review before changing canonical identity.
checks: Embedding similarity alone never auto-merges skills.
Specializations remain linked rather than collapsed.
Duplicate findings include evidence spans.
failures: Treating shared headings as semantic duplication.
Keeping aliases as independent skills to inflate counts.

title: Promoting Skill Providers
description: Use when a quarantined or candidate provider requests validated, stable, or certified status and must prove current trust, quality, compatibility, freshness, and mapping integrity.
antiTriggers: provider content or source revision changed after evaluation
the requester supplies metrics without a trusted eval receipt
steps: Verify immutable provider digest, signature, license, scans, and source revision.
Load trusted evaluation and mapping-attestation receipts.
Apply maturity thresholds and risk-specific reviewer separation.
Commit status change atomically with expiry and audit events.
checks: Promotion uses stored receipts, not caller-provided scores.
Critical blockers always win.
Tenant admin cannot mutate global built-ins.
failures: Using stars as trust proof.
Promoting after only static schema validation.

title: Expiring Stale Skills
description: Use when provider sources, tool APIs, model behavior, security assumptions, evaluators, or compatibility windows may have become outdated since the last successful validation.
antiTriggers: the provider has a current immutable source and unexpired evaluation
historical archived providers that cannot route
steps: Evaluate source revision, observed date, compatibility window, and last eval.
Identify dependency or policy changes that force early revalidation.
Move stale providers out of stable routing without deleting history.
Schedule bounded re-sync, scan, and evaluation work.
checks: Expired providers cannot appear in executable bundles.
Routes explain freshness exclusion.
Revalidation preserves previous failure history.
failures: Leaving stable status forever.
Refreshing timestamps without rerunning compatibility tests.

title: Learning from Agent Failures
description: Use when repeated agent, route, tool, context, or verification failures reveal a reusable technique gap rather than a one-off project defect.
antiTriggers: the failure is caused by a known code bug
one isolated failure has no reproducible pattern
steps: Cluster failures by invariant, rationalization, missing context, and tool boundary.
Trace each cluster to skill, router, policy, or runtime responsibility.
Create a minimal RED scenario reproducing the reusable gap.
Propose a skill or code change without auto-promoting it.
checks: Learning artifacts cite raw failure receipts.
Project-specific details are removed safely.
No production rule changes without evaluation.
failures: Turning every bug into a new skill.
Allowing continuous learning to edit stable content directly.

title: Certifying Release Evidence
description: Use when a source archive, package, container, skill registry, or product release needs reproducible proof bound to the exact bytes being distributed.
antiTriggers: an uncommitted experiment has no release subject
verification ran on a different source tree or archive
steps: Freeze the source manifest and all release subjects.
Run mandatory tests, audits, protocol checks, and archive acceptance independently.
Generate SBOM, provenance, checksums, and detached signatures.
Publish claims boundaries and residual risks alongside evidence.
checks: Archive can verify without a .git directory.
Evidence names exact source and archive digests.
Private signing material is not packaged.
failures: Signing a report that does not bind archive bytes.
Calling a docs-only adapter certified.
